title: Stripe-packed checkpoint layout + kernel-swap workspace scheduler
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: GPU peak working-set reduced (~18%) via stripe-packed checkpoint layout and dynamic kernel-swap scheduler; KV prefetch timing adjusted to avoid transient spikes; opt-in rollout behind runtime flag
description:
Motivation: Runtime peak GPU memory for long-context and multi-concurrent sessions is dominated by transient activation checkpoints and scratch buffers. Existing arena packing reduces fragmentation but still leaves worst-case peaks when large kernels and KV cache operations coincide. This PR introduces two complementary techniques: 1) a stripe-packed checkpoint layout that packs checkpointed activation fragments into tightly interleaved stripes to reduce per-kernel working set, and 2) a kernel-swap workspace scheduler that defers non-critical kernel workspace allocations and opportunistically swaps packed checkpoint stripes to a hotset buffer during safe epochs. The result is lower transient GPU footprint with negligible throughput impact for typical workloads.

Design summary: The changeset contains: - runtime/allocator/stripe_packer.{cpp,h}: new packing allocator that writes checkpoints as interleaved stripe pages and maintains a compact index. The layout is guided by per-layer size histograms so larger activations are split across stripes to avoid single large contiguous allocations. - runtime/scheduler/kernel_swap_scheduler.{cpp,h}: a lightweight scheduler that tracks upcoming kernel workspace needs (based on compiled kernel descriptors) and introduces micro-delays or pre-eviction of low-priority checkpoint stripes when a high-water mark is predicted. It integrates with existing continuous-batching signals to avoid affecting short-latency requests. - runtime/kv/cache_timing_adjuster.{cpp,h}: small heuristics that shift eager KV prefetchs slightly earlier or later (configurable window) to avoid simultaneous peaks with planned large kernel work. - runtime/config/runtime_flags.yaml: feature flag stripe_packed_ckpt + kernel_swap_mode with three modes (off, conservative, aggressive) to control rollout. - tests/benchmarks/stripe_packed_peak_mem.py: microbench harness used for the numbers below. - doc/ops/stripe_pack_notes.md: operator-facing notes and recommended knob settings.

Compatibility and safety: All new behavior is gated behind runtime flags and default to conservative mode in hosted. The stripe layout preserves on-disk and in-memory checkpoint semantics (index translates to original offsets) so no model changes are required. Kernel-swap scheduler only defers workspace allocations when allocation would otherwise fail the memory check; in conservative mode it only triggers for kernels > 32MB workspace.

Benchmarks and results: Measured on p4d.24xlarge with a long-context transformer (64k tokens synthetic) under mixed small/large batch traffic. Numbers are 95th percentile across runs: - peak GPU working-set: baseline 43.1GB -> stripe+swap 35.3GB (~18% reduction) - sustained throughput: baseline 112 seq/s -> stripe+swap 118 seq/s (+5%) due to reduced GC/evict churn in KV - 99p latency increase: +3ms in aggressive mode, <1ms in conservative mode - KV miss spikes reduced on concurrent load by ~40% (observed in trace samples)

Testing and QA: - Unit tests for stripe_packer allocation/compactness and index correctness. - Integration tests for kernel_swap_scheduler under synthetic batch traces. - End-to-end smoke runs against hosted canary with conservative flags enabled. - Load tests for KV timing behavior in the benchmark lab. CI includes unit + integration + e2e canary checks; initial CI run had a lint failure which was fixed in commit 3.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind flags. 2) Enable conservative mode in dedicated lab for 2 weeks and monitor peak memory and 95th latency. 3) Enable conservative for a small percentage of hosted traffic. 4) If metrics look good, enable aggressive mode in private clusters where customers opt-in.

Related work: follows on ideas from ENG-2170 (arena packing) but focuses on temporal co-location and ordering rather than raw fragmentation. Also complements KV windowed eviction work (see SUP-512) by smoothing timing interactions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Benchmarks present - [x] Feature flags added - [x] Docs for operators - [x] Security review N/A (no external surface change)

Notes: this PR intentionally keeps the stripe packer conservative in memory movement; a follow-up will add a compact-on-idle pass that further reduces fragmentation but requires pinned-memory staging to avoid host<->device thrash.
